# Results — Study 485 (STARC Bands)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **price
mean-reverts from the STARC bands: a close below the lower band snaps back toward the SMA** —
encoded as a mechanical rule. The center is a 6-bar SMA of the close; the bands are
`SMA ± 2·ATR(15)` with Wilder's ATR (all causal, trailing only). A long fires on the first close
**below the lower band**, entered at the **next close** (one documented lag), and we measure the
forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Bands | center = SMA(6) of close; bands = center ± **2 · ATR(15)** (Wilder ATR; all trailing) |
| Entries | **241** mechanical lower-band pierces pooled across the 5 tapes |
| Timing / costs | bands are causal (no look-ahead); enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per pierce |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument channel study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only the
> drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

## The signal — lower-band pierce vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch pierce-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = pierce − random.

| horizon | n | pierce | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (pierce−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 241 | +1.3 bps   | 60% | +0.05 | +8.5 bps   | **−7.1 bps**   | −0.7 bps   | −0.25 | 0.801 |
| 10-day | 241 | +22.9 bps  | 60% | +0.65 | +51.5 bps  | **−28.6 bps**  | +20.9 bps  | −0.80 | 0.423 |
| 20-day | 241 | +115.8 bps | 67% | +2.70 | +45.5 bps  | **+70.4 bps**  | +113.8 bps | +1.46 | 0.145 |
| 60-day | 240 | +383.3 bps | 75% | +5.54 | +124.6 bps | **+258.8 bps** | +381.3 bps | +3.34 | 0.001 |

Read it carefully. At **5 and 10 days** the lower-band pierce is *at or below* a drift-matched
random entry (Δ = −7.1 / −28.6 bps; Welch *t* negative) — the famous "reversion" does **not**
beat throwing darts in the short run, exactly where a mean-reversion claim should be strongest.
At **20 days** the gap is positive but not significant (Welch *t* = +1.46, *p* = 0.145). Only at
**60 days** does the pierce clear the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar (Welch *t* = +3.34, *p* = 0.001) — a
long-horizon effect that is the *opposite* of the snap-back the rule advertises and that, as the
placebo below shows, owes nothing to the bands' geometry.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — incoherent across the basket

| ticker | entries | pierce | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (pierce−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 51 | +110.6 bps | +1.32 | +46.1 bps | **+64.5 bps** |
| QQQ | 43 | +61.5 bps  | +0.55 | +88.2 bps | **−26.7 bps** |
| IWM | 33 | −32.0 bps  | −0.20 | +2.7 bps  | **−34.7 bps** |
| DIA | 57 | +149.7 bps | +1.86 | +11.5 bps | **+138.2 bps** |
| GLD | 57 | +213.2 bps | +3.42 | +78.9 bps | **+134.3 bps** |

The 20-day delta is **negative in 2 of 5 names** (QQQ, IWM) and the only big positive *t* (GLD,
+3.42) is on the one cross-asset, non-equity tape. No coherent cross-sectional pattern — the
hallmark of an effect riding on each tape's idiosyncratic drift after a high-volatility drawdown,
not a reproducible band edge.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the ATR, nothing changes

The decisive "does the band geometry matter?" test: keep the SMA center and the price **marginal**,
but **permute the ATR series** so the band half-width at each date is a random width from the
sample, destroying the volatility scaling that defines a STARC pierce. If price genuinely reverted
from *these specific volatility-scaled lines*, the scramble would collapse the result.

| test | observed lower-band 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY shuffled-ATR bands | +110.6 bps | **0.964** | 500 |

**96% of scrambled-ATR bands match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.964). The STARC bands carry no
information — a random-width envelope around the same SMA does just as well. "Price respects the
STARC band" is busted: it's the SMA-relative dip plus drift, not the ATR scaling, doing whatever
little work there is.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real bounce

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* lower-band reversion (knob `edge`), the same lower-band
rule behaves exactly as it must — so the flat short-horizon real-tape result is a genuine "nothing
there", not a dead detector. (Symmetric fat-tailed innovations make pierces frequent; a per-bar
Jensen correction keeps the `edge=0` arm a fair coin.)

| planted edge | n | pierce | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no bounce) | 48 | +79.4 bps  | 54% | +0.89 |
| **0.50** (real planted bounce) | 44 | +159.5 bps | 61% | **+2.07** |

With no planted bounce the control sits below the *t* = 2 bar (no false positive, win ≈ coin); a
real planted bounce lights up at *t* = +2.07 with a 61% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The lower-band pierce does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline at
  the horizons where a reversion claim lives (5d Δ = −7.1, 10d Δ = −28.6 bps; Welch *t* negative;
  20d *p* = 0.145). It clears *t* ≥ 2 only at **60 days** (Welch *t* = +3.34) — one horizon out of
  four, a long-hold drift effect that is the opposite of a "snap-back". The big one-sample *t*'s
  (20d +2.70, 60d +5.54) are mostly beta. A single-horizon pass with three failures and an
  incoherent cross-section is, at best, weak.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The only horizon that beats random (60d) survives neither the
  geometry placebo (the bands are irrelevant) nor the cross-section (negative in QQQ/IWM); it is a
  drift effect you would capture more cheaply by holding the index. Net-of-cost it barely moves the
  short horizons. There is a number that clears the bar, but nothing robust to deploy.
- **"Does the band touch forecast reversion?" — BUSTED.** The shuffled-ATR placebo leaves the
  result intact (*p* = 0.964): random-width envelopes do as well as the real STARC bands, so the
  ATR scaling — the entire point of the indicator — carries no forecasting information. The band
  touch does not forecast reversion; whatever long-horizon drift shows up is SMA-relative dip-buying
  plus beta, not the STARC channel.
